\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Influence}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Applications.Influence
\section{Overview}
Hypercontractivity bounds stable coordinate influences and the low Fourier levels of indicator functions. The level-one estimate has the sharp logarithmic coefficient obtained from linear correlations.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Indicator noise stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.indicator_stability_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.setIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.small_set_expansion, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.volume, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p254-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p254-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b001
}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ and $0<\rho\le1$. Then under the uniform cube law $\mathbb E[fT_\rho f]\le(\mathbb Ef)^{2/(1+\rho)}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indicator correlation with linear forms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.indicator_linear_form_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.indicator_innerProduct_le_of_mgf, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.rademacher_mgf_le, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $0$ and $1$,
with uniform expectation $\alpha=\mathbb E f>0$. For real coefficients $(a_i)_{i=1}^n$
satisfying $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, the squared correlation with the sign-valued linear form
obeys
\[\left(\mathbb E\left[f(x)\sum_i a_i(-1)^{x_i}\right]\right)^2\le2\alpha^2\log(1/\alpha).\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noisy influence as a derivative norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noisyInfluence_eq_sq_norm_derivative}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourierCoeff_derivative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose, BooleanAnalysis.derivative, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct_self_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_self_adjoint, BooleanAnalysis.stability_formula, KKL.noisyInfluence}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $i$ be a
coordinate, and let $\rho\ge0$. Then the noisy influence of $f$ at coordinate $i$ equals
$\|T_{\sqrt{\rho}}D_i f\|_2^2$, where $(D_i
f)(x)=\bigl(f(x^{i\mapsto0})-f(x^{i\mapsto1})\bigr)/2$ and the norm is taken with
respect to the uniform measure on the cube.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$, let $i\in[n]$, and let
$p\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $p>0$. Then $\mathbb E|D_i f|^p=\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$, with uniform
expectation on the cube, where $D_i f(x)=(f(x^{i\mapsto 0})-f(x^{i\mapsto 1}))/2$ and
$\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]=\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^i))^2/4]$, with $x^i$ obtained by flipping
coordinate $i$.
\end{lemma}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b004}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\\in\\mathbb N$, let $f:\\{0,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$ take values in $\\{-1,1\\}$,
let $i\\in[n]$, and let $0\\le\\rho\\le1$. Then the noisy coordinate influence satisfies
$I_i^{(\\rho)}(f)\\le\\mathrm{Inf}_i(f)^{2/(1+\\rho)}$, where
$I_i^{(\\rho)}(f)=\\sum_{S\\ni i}\\rho^{|S|-1}\\widehat f(S)^2$ and
$\\mathrm{Inf}_i(f)=\\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^i))^2/4]$ under the uniform cube measure.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n\\in\\mathbb N$, let $f:\\{0,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$ take values in $\\{-1,1\\}$,
and let $i\\in[n]$. Then $I_i^{(1/3)}(f)\\le\\mathrm{Inf}_i(f)^{3/2}$, where
$I_i^{(1/3)}(f)=\\sum_{S\\ni i}(1/3)^{|S|-1}\\widehat f(S)^2$ and
$\\mathrm{Inf}_i(f)=\\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^i))^2/4]$ under the uniform cube measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Weighted low-level Fourier bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.weighted_fourierWeightUpTo_le_stability}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, and let $\rho\in\bbr$ satisfy
$0\le\rho\le1$. If $\widehat f(S)$ denotes the Walsh–Fourier coefficient of $f$ at
$S\subseteq[n]$ and $T_\rho$ is the noise operator, then
\[\rho^k\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq[n]\\|S|\le k}}\widehat f(S)^2\le\langle f,T_\rho
f\rangle.\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indicator power and exponential estimate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.indicator_rpow_le_sq_mul_exp}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For real numbers $\alpha,\rho$ with $0<\alpha\le1$ and $\rho\ge0$, one has
\[\alpha^{2/(1+\rho)}\le\alpha^2\exp\!\left(2\rho\log(1/\alpha)\right).\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Optimization of a level bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.level_k_optimization}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.indicator_rpow_le_sq_mul_exp}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b006}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha,W\in\mathbb R$, with $0<\alpha\le1$, and let $k$ be a positive natural
number satisfying $k\le2\log(1/\alpha)$. Suppose that for every real $\rho$ with
$0<\rho\le1$, $\rho^kW\le\alpha^{2/(1+\rho)}$. Then
$W\le\left(\frac{2e}{k}\log(1/\alpha)\right)^k\alpha^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier weight bound for indicators]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.level_k_inequality}

  {BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.level_k_optimization}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b006}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k$ be natural numbers and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $0$
and $1$. Write $\alpha=\mathbb E[f]$, and assume $\alpha>0$, $k>0$, and
$k\le2\log(1/\alpha)$. Then the Fourier weight on levels at most $k$ satisfies
$\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2\le\left(\frac{2e}{k}\log(1/\alpha)\right)^k\alpha^2$,
with Fourier coefficients and expectation under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Level-one indicator inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.level_one_inequality}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.indicator_linear_form_sq_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.exists_unit_linear_form, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_mono, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p126-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p273-b005
}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ have uniform mean $\alpha>0$. Then $\sum_{|S|=1}\widehat f(S)^2\le2\alpha^2\log(1/\alpha)$.
\end{theorem}
